inputs.share_count_basis: 443,217,637 Shares issued and fully paid at 3 July 2026 (H1 2026 interim, share capital note); dilutive potential shares round to nil (diluted WASO = basic WASO 446m). Held FLAT: SBC (~0.2% of revenue) is expensed in the flows. The up-to-EUR1bn Feb-26/Feb-27 buyback is a capital-return choice and is value-neutral in this model, not credited as per-share accretion.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company net debt at 3 July 2026 is EUR10,284m (adjusted total borrowings 12,278 incl. hedge FV 93 and other -4, less cash 1,753 and short-term investments 241). Lease obligations (500 non-current + 174 current = 674) are REMOVED because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B): borrowings ex leases 11,604, net debt 9,610. H1 balance sheet is seasonally heavier than December (interim dividend EUR365m and EUR503m buyback paid in H1).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F/annual report cash flow statement share-based payment add-back EUR47m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed; small treasury-share purchases for employee plans (EUR17m in H1 2026) are covered by rounding sbc_pct up to 0.25% in the forward path.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: CCEP is a net-debt company (EUR9.6bn ex leases), so there is no cash pile to double-count. Interest received sits in investing and interest paid in financing, so reported FCF (OCF - capex) is already pre-financing.
inputs.fx_note: EUR->USD 1.1392 (Yahoo EURUSD=X, 2026-09-25 close). All flows and per-share values are computed in EUR and converted to USD at this rate so that intrinsic_value / weighted_iv compare with the NASDAQ price. Parity check: Euronext Amsterdam CCEP.AS EUR88.40 x 1.1392 = USD100.70 vs NASDAQ USD101.73 (1.0% gap, explained by Amsterdam closing ~5.5 hours before NASDAQ). Direction confirmed. refresh_price.py moves the price, never this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built WACC 7.0%: 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta ~0.75 x 5.5% ERP = cost of equity ~6.8-7.0%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.5% on ~20% D/EV (EUR9.6bn net debt vs ~EUR39.6bn market cap). Arithmetic WACC ~6.0%; rounded up to 7.0% for the APS emerging-market share (Indonesia, Philippines, PNG ~10% of revenue) and TCCC dependence. Same WACC in all three scenarios - risk is charged in the flows, once.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease principal (EUR162m FY2025) plus lease interest (EUR23m) = EUR185m = 0.89% of revenue charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease obligations (EUR674m at 3 Jul 2026) excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (~3.5% of revenue vs 4.4% total) so the lease is charged once in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of CCEAP Philippines, owned 60/40 with Aboitiz Equity Ventures). NCI charged once, in the bridge: -EUR800m (NCI share of comparable after-tax operating profit EUR40m FY2025, ~EUR48m run-rate on H1-26's EUR24m, at ~17x). Book NCI is EUR487m; the market-value figure is used because the Philippines is still growing into its ~10% EBIT target.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: a franchise bottler is an operating company whose value is its free-cash-flow stream (not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco); non-US adaptations applied (EUR WACC, EUR flows vs USD quote, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC near zero). First valuation of this ticker - no prior model to match. FY2021 (Amatil, +30% revenue) and FY2024 (Philippines, +12%) are acquisition step-changes; the 5yr revenue CAGR of 14.5% is therefore not used - the forward path is anchored on FY2026 guidance (+3-4% revenue, ~+7% comparable operating profit) and organic NARTD growth. EBITDA margin in the drivers is BEFORE SBC (reported EBITDA 17.8% + SBC 0.2%); FY2025 reported EBITDA includes EUR15m items impacting comparability and accelerated Beam Suntory amortisation in D&A (non-recurring). Year-1 check: engine FY2026 unlevered owner FCF ~EUR2.0bn, which after ~EUR150m after-tax net interest ties to ~EUR1.85bn comparable FCF against guidance of at least EUR1.7bn (FY2025 actual 1,836 included ~EUR170m of one-off property disposals). Buyback: repurchaser (EUR1,006m FY2025, EUR503m H1 2026), so the flat count is funded. Working capital capture 0: a bottler runs negative working capital, but its growth inflow is small and not relied on.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest in CCEAP Philippines (40% Aboitiz) at ~17x NCI earnings
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 interim: profit attributable to NCI EUR24m per half; FY2025 comparable NCI EUR40m; book NCI EUR487m at 3 Jul 2026

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 revenue guidance midpoint (+3-4%); all CAGRs are distorted by acquisitions (Amatil FY2021, Philippines FY2024) and the FY2020 COVID base
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.4% 5yr, 1.7% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue (14.5%) and EPS (31.3%) CAGRs. Equity is suppressed by ~50% dividend payout plus EUR1bn/yr buybacks since FY2025 and is not a growth signal; revenue and EPS 5yr CAGRs are inflated by M&A and a COVID FY2020 base. None is used; guidance anchors the path.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (FCF - SBC) CAGRs track reported FCF closely because SBC is ~0.2% of revenue - SBC is not paying for growth here. The 3yr FCF decline reflects the FY2022 low-capex peak (capex 3.5% of revenue) normalising to 4.5% and higher cash tax, not deterioration.

base.rationale: FY2026 on guidance (revenue +3.5%, comparable OP ~+7% -> EBITDA pre-SBC 18.3%); organic 3.5-4% (Europe price/mix +2-3%, SE Asia high single digit) fading to 2.5%; ~15bp/yr margin expansion from productivity, energy/zero mix and Philippines margin build to 19.2% (comparable OP ~14.6% vs 13.4% FY2025); capex elevated 4.8% for the 2027 Philippines plant and the EUR1bn capacity programme then 4.3%; cash tax 23% (FY2023-25 cash taxes ~21-22% of OP) ramping to 24.5% so no deferred-tax shelter is perpetuated.

scenario_narratives.base: CCEP delivers its FY2026 guide (revenue +3-4%, comparable operating profit ~+7%) and then settles into a mid-single-digit-minus top line: Western Europe grows 2-3% on price/mix with zero-sugar, energy (Monster) and sports offsetting flat full-sugar sparkling volume, while Indonesia and the Philippines grow high single digits as the 2027 Philippines plant and new route-to-market add capacity. Productivity (Manila shared services, S/4HANA, revenue growth management) buys ~15bp a year of margin until comparable OP margin reaches ~14.6%. Capex runs high through the Philippines build then normalises; buybacks and a ~50% payout return the cash but do not add value in the model.
scenario_narratives.bull: Southeast Asia becomes a genuine second growth engine - the Philippines reaches and passes its ~10% EBIT target, Indonesia sparkling recovers - and energy/zero-sugar mix keeps European price/mix at the top of the range, so revenue compounds at 4.5-5% for several years and EBITDA margin reaches 20% (comparable OP ~15.5%) as concentrate-cost inflation stays low-single-digit and efficiency programmes compound.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sugar taxes (France 2025, further UK/Australian changes) and packaging/EPR levies keep eroding sparkling volumes; TCCC lifts concentrate pricing under the incidence model, grocers and private label squeeze promotions, and Indonesia stays weak. Revenue grows ~2% after FY2026, EBITDA margin gives back ~100bp to 17.3% (FY2022-23 levels), capex stays at 4.5-4.8% to defend the network, and OECD Pillar Two / higher UK rates push cash tax to 25.5%. Terminal value capped at 16x for a structurally ex-growth bottler.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%: no solvency or refinancing risk (investment-grade, 2.6x net debt/EBITDA), but the bear drivers - sugar tax, EPR, TCCC concentrate pricing - are regulatory and counterparty levers CCEP does not control and are already visible in France. Base 55%: a mature staple with reaffirmed guidance and a long record of hitting it deserves a heavier central weight than the 50% default. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs two independent things to go right at once - SE Asia margin convergence and sustained European price/mix above inflation.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A franchise bottler is a low-growth, capital-intensive cash compounder whose economics are set partly by The Coca-Cola Company. Value it on unlevered owner FCF after the full lease payment and SBC, on guidance-anchored organic growth rather than acquisition-inflated CAGRs, at a EUR-built WACC, then convert to USD for the NASDAQ quote. The buyback and dividend are how the cash is returned, not a source of value.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominance: at 7% WACC and 2.5% growth Gordon (~23x) exceeds the 20x cap, so the cap binds in every scenario and ~56-65% of enterprise value sits in the terminal value
WACC sensitivity: each 1pp of WACC moves base value by roughly 15-20% for a long-duration staple
TCCC concentrate pricing and incidence-model changes directly set the EBITDA margin path
EUR/USD: the USD per-share value moves 1:1 with the rate; the EUR value is the economic one
Sugar tax / EPR regulation across France, UK, Australia and Southeast Asia
Acquisition risk: CCEP has done two transformative deals in five years; another (e.g. further TCCC-owned bottler refranchising) would reset the path
